objectives.text: Explain how an index speeds up a lookup and what it costs on writes and storage
Create a B-tree index, including a multicolumn index, that matches a described query
Identify the indexes PostgreSQL creates automatically for PRIMARY KEY and UNIQUE constraints

minutes.basis: intake-target: no artifact.html exists yet, so modeledP50 and modeledWorstPath are intake planning targets, not estimator output. modeledP50: the core target P50 of 7.0 minutes, from course-1 measured estimator P50 (tools/timing/estimate_reading.py sha256 0deca96bf5e367aeae51a82abdbd4b6ce0d0289ecc9868c9eff3701016edf96f) for comparable core pages. modeledWorstPath: 10.0 minutes, the target P50 times 1.42, the mean course-1 ratio of recorded worst-required-route to estimator P50. budget and aboutLabel: ceil(max(modeledP50, modeledWorstPath)) = 10 per the new-course rule in docs/tools/validators.md (Reading time, T14). The module PR replaces both modeled values with the estimator P50 and the modeled worst required route of the authored page and raises the budget if the honest minimum is higher; it never compresses it. See evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/intake.md, section Minute budgets.
